q1.question: Why Postgres and not Mongo or Firebase?
q1.answer: Postgres is predictable, ACID, and scales without surprises. Firebase looks easy at first but locks you in and gets expensive fast. Mongo is fine for very specific cases, but most SaaS is relational — joins, transactions, reports. Postgres is the right answer 90% of the time.

q2.question: What kind of apps have you built?
q2.answer: Complete LMS with courses + payments (PrimeX Academy), custom admin panel for member management (Gotten Gym), client portals with project tracking, internal B2B dashboards. If it fits in a browser tab, we build it.

q3.question: How much does a custom app cost?
q3.answer: Functional MVP from €4,000. Full SaaS with multi-tenant, billing and admin panel between €6,000 and €15,000. Fixed price on signature — no variations on you.

q4.question: How long does it take?
q4.answer: Functional MVP 4-6 weeks. Mature product with auth, billing, admin panel and multi-tenant: 8-12 weeks. Fixed timeline on the first call.

q5.question: What about hosting and costs?
q5.answer: Vercel for the frontend (free tier until real traffic), Neon or Supabase for Postgres, Cloudflare R2 for assets. Typical monthly cost for a medium app: €50-200. I leave everything configured and documented for you to scale calmly.

q6.question: Post-launch support?
q6.answer: 30 days of free post-launch support included. After that, monthly retainer from €400/month for maintenance + iteration. Or one-off hours at €80/h, no commitment.

q1.question: Shopify or custom-built?
q1.answer: It depends. Shopify wins when your logic fits the ecosystem and you want to ship fast — perfect up to 7-figure revenue. Custom-built wins when your model is B2B, you have complex catalog logic, or you don't want to pay Shopify commissions forever. We evaluate it on the first call.

q4.question: Will I lose SEO if I migrate?
q4.answer: Not if it's done right. We map every old URL, 301-redirect to the new ones, preserve meta tags and schemas, and monitor Search Console for 30 days post-launch. In recent migrations we've kept 100% of organic traffic — and improved rankings thanks to the performance boost.

f5.description: 10-year-old PHP apps, inherited internal systems, unmaintained stacks. Module-by-module rewrite — no big-bang, no business interruption.

q1.question: Are you going to tank my Google rankings?
q1.answer: No. We do a full SEO audit before touching anything, map every old URL to its new equivalent with a permanent 301, keep metadata and structured data, and monitor Search Console for 4 weeks post-launch. Most of our migrations gain organic traffic — they don't lose it.

q2.question: How do you migrate data without losing anything?
q2.answer: We export everything cold (posts, products, users, media, comments), transform it to the new CMS structure and upload it to staging for your validation before touching the live site. We diff content to guarantee 100% parity before the switch.

q3.question: How much does migrating cost?
q3.answer: Corporate site (< 200 pages): €2,500 - €5,000. Large blog or digital media (< 2,000 posts): €5,000 - €10,000. E-commerce with thousands of products: €8,000 - €18,000. Complex legacy app: from €15,000. Fixed budget after the initial audit.

q4.question: How long does it take?
q4.answer: Corporate site: 2-3 weeks. Blog or media: 3-5 weeks. E-commerce: 4-8 weeks. Legacy app: 8-16 weeks with module releases. We always launch on Tuesday or Wednesday — never a Friday.

q5.question: And if something goes wrong on launch day?
q5.answer: We have a rollback plan ready: if anything looks off in the first hours (ranking drop, 500s, broken data), we revert to the previous site in 5 minutes by switching DNS. That's why we always keep the old site alive on a subdomain for the first 2 weeks.

q6.question: Do you keep the old URLs or does everything change?
q6.answer: Your call. If the old URLs work SEO-wise, we replicate them 1:1 on the new site. If they're badly structured, we redesign them with permanent 301s — Google reassigns equity in 4-8 weeks with no measurable loss.

manifesto.label: // MANIFESTO
body: I started solo. I'm still solo. Not to save money — by choice.
Agencies of 20 people need to sell to 20 people to survive. They take briefs that don't fit, impossible deadlines, clients going nowhere. The team grows and the average work drops.
A boutique studio works the other way. Every project goes through one head, one hand. What ships is exactly what was in my head on day one. No broken-telephone effect.
There are 30 or 40 boutique studios in the world I admire that work like this. Slow to scale, fast to execute. Exactly what the clients I fit with need.

privacy.label: // PRIVACY POLICY
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Bellostas Studio takes your privacy seriously. This document explains what data we collect, why, and what rights you have over it. We comply with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and Spanish Organic Law 3/2018 on Data Protection and Digital Rights (LOPDGDD).

ul: Controller: Antonio Bellostas Fetysov
Spanish tax ID (NIF): 18060373Z
Address: C. Fornillos, 13, 22005 Huesca, Spain
Email: info@bellostas.studio

blocks.p: Given its size and activity, Bellostas Studio is not legally required to appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO). Any privacy question can be sent directly to the email above.
We collect only the data that is strictly needed to deliver the service or reply to your request:

ul: Identification data (first name, last name) when you submit a form or book a call.
Contact data (email, optional phone, company) to reply or manage the project.
The content of your message (project brief, rough budget, etc.).
Technical browsing data (anonymised IP, browser, OS, page views) when you accept analytics cookies.

blocks.p: We do not collect special categories of data (health, beliefs, sexual orientation, etc.) or data from minors under 14.
We process your data for the following purposes, each with its own legal basis:

ul: Reply to your contact or quote request — basis: your explicit consent when submitting the form (Art. 6.1.a GDPR).
Manage the contractual relationship if we end up working together — basis: contract performance (Art. 6.1.b GDPR).
Comply with tax and accounting obligations — basis: legal obligation (Art. 6.1.c GDPR).
Measure and improve the site through aggregate analytics — basis: your prior consent via the cookie banner (Art. 6.1.a GDPR).
Contact data and pre-contract communications: up to 12 months from the last message, unless you ask us to delete it sooner.
Active client data: throughout the contractual relationship and afterwards for the legally required periods (6 years for tax records, up to 10 years for anti-money-laundering rules).
Aggregate analytics data: up to 14 months (GA4 default).

blocks.p: To deliver the service we rely on providers that comply with GDPR and with whom we have (or will have, once activated) the relevant data processing agreement:

ul: Netcup GmbH (Germany, EU) — website hosting. Data stored within the EEA.
Cal.com Inc. (EU instance) — call booking management. Data processed on European servers.
Resend Inc. (USA) — transactional email delivery (once enabled). Listed under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework with Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) in place.
Google Ireland Ltd. — Google Analytics 4. Aggregate data, anonymised IP, US transfer covered by the Data Privacy Framework and SCCs.
Bellostas Studio internal CRM — storage of contacts and sales opportunities. Hosted on the controller's own European infrastructure.

blocks.p: We do not sell or transfer your data to third parties for purposes other than those described above.

Some processors are based outside the EEA (Resend, Google). These transfers are made under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or, otherwise, through Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission, in accordance with Article 46 GDPR.
You can exercise the following rights over your data at any time:

ul: Access: know what data we hold about you.
Rectification: correct inaccurate data.
Erasure: ask us to delete data we no longer need.
Objection: object to a specific processing activity.
Restriction: ask us to freeze processing in certain cases.
Portability: receive your data in a structured format to move it to another controller.
Withdraw any consent you have given, without retroactive effect.

blocks.p: To exercise any of these rights, write to info@bellostas.studio attaching an ID document. We will respond within one month at most.
If you feel your request has not been properly handled, you can file a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (www.aepd.es).

We apply reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect your data: TLS encryption on all communications, access restricted to authorised personnel, regular backups and ongoing supplier review.

We may update this policy to reflect legal or service changes. When changes are substantial, we will notify users on the site. The date of the latest version is always shown at the top of the document.

cookies.label: // COOKIE POLICY
cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.intro: This document explains what cookies are, which ones we use on bellostas.studio and how you can manage them at any time. It complies with Article 22.2 of the Spanish LSSI-CE and with the guidelines from the Spanish Data Protection Agency.

blocks.p: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. They make it possible to recognise the user, remember preferences or measure how the site is used. They are not viruses, do not access other files on your device and do not collect sensitive information.
We classify cookies in three categories:

ul: Essential — required for the site to work (remembering your language and your own cookie choice). They do not require consent and cannot be disabled.
Analytics — let us understand, in aggregate, how the site is being used so we can improve design and content. They require your explicit consent.
Marketing — we don't currently use marketing cookies. If we ever do, this policy will be updated first.

blocks.p: These are the cookies active on this site:

rows: Distinguish users and measure aggregate use (GA4)

blocks.p: Analytics cookies are only loaded after you explicitly accept them through the banner. Until then, no data is sent to Google or any third party.

You can change your preferences at any time by clicking the "Open cookie settings" button just below this text. You can also delete or block cookies from your browser settings (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).
Rejecting all non-analytics cookies does not affect browsing: the site works exactly the same.
We may update this policy if we add or remove cookies. When the changes are relevant, we will notify users on the site and request your consent again if necessary.
